non_member.label: Not a UN member
non_member.explanation: Taiwan is not a member of the United Nations: since General Assembly resolution 2758 (1971) China's seat is held by the People's Republic of China, and only a small number of states recognise Taiwan. It has its own government, tax system and residence rules, which is what this site compares.

data.name: Taiwan
data.summary: Taiwan taxes individuals on Taiwan-source income at up to 40%. Foreign income, including foreign capital gains and dividends, is reached only by the 20% alternative minimum tax (income basic tax), which applies when foreign income is TWD 1 million or more and basic income exceeds TWD 7.5 million; for a family of this size that is close to a flat 20%. Taiwan listed-share gains are exempt (0.3% transaction tax), and Taiwan dividends cost up to 28%. Estate and gift tax (10%-20%) reaches only Taiwan-situs property of foreign nationals. There is no wealth tax and no US tax treaty.

regimes.name: Taiwan resident
regimes.description: Taiwan-source income at 5%-40%; foreign income only through the 20% income basic tax above TWD 7.5 million; estate tax on Taiwan assets only for foreigners.
regimes.eligibility: Foreigners are resident if present 183 days or more in a calendar year.

capital_gains.summary: Taiwan taxes individuals' Taiwan-source income at 5%-40%. Gains on Taiwan securities are exempt from income tax (a 0.3% securities transaction tax applies to share sales). Foreign-source income, including gains on foreign securities and foreign property, is outside the regular income tax but enters the alternative minimum tax (income basic tax, IBT) at 20% once a resident's foreign income is TWD 1 million or more and basic income exceeds TWD 7.5 million, with a credit for foreign tax. Taiwan real estate acquired from 2016 is under the consolidated house and land income tax: 45% (2 years or less), 35% (2-5), 20% (5-10), 15% (over 10 years); a self-used home qualifies for TWD 4 million exemption and 10% above it.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: IBT: the household deducts TWD 7.5 million once from its basic income and pays 20% of the rest (Income Basic Tax Act art. 13, whose text says TWD 6 million, raised to 7.5 million by the Ministry of Finance's CPI adjustment under art. 3(2); amount confirmed on the Ministry of Finance portal, updated 2026-04-15). A household's foreign income under TWD 1 million is left out entirely; at TWD 1 million or more all of it counts (art. 12). The art. 3(2) adjustment applies when the CPI has risen 10% or more since the last adjustment, in TWD 100,000 steps.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: IBT is payable only to the extent it exceeds regular income tax. For the family's scale (foreign income far above TWD 7.5 million) the effective rate approaches 20%. Gains on certain unlisted/privately placed securities are IBT add-back items.

The 2026 IBT deduction of TWD 7.5 million was confirmed from the Ministry of Finance portal text (updated 2026-04-15), not from a 2026 announcement.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Foreign gains: 20% IBT. Domestic listed: income-tax exempt, 0.3% securities transaction tax on proceeds = 0.6% of the gain assuming the gain is half the proceeds. Private business sale (unlisted Taiwan company): assumed to fall into IBT at 20% (low confidence). Local real estate held over 10 years: 15%. Headline 45% = short-holding house and land rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Securities gains remain exempt even for frequent traders (general knowledge); property dealing businesses are taxed under the house and land rules.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: House and land tax rates fall with holding period (above).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign income is taxed only through IBT (20%) and only for residents (183 days or domiciled).

dividends.summary: Taiwan dividends of resident individuals are either included in consolidated income (up to 40%) with an 8.5% credit capped at TWD 80,000, or taxed separately at 28%. Foreign dividends are foreign-source income, outside regular tax but included in IBT at 20% (same thresholds as above) with credit for foreign tax.
dividends.important_exceptions: Dividend options of Income Tax Act art. 15: an 8.5% credit capped at TWD 80,000 per return on consolidated income, or a separate flat 28% (English text of the Act opened 2026-10-16).

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: separate 28% option (better than 40% less the capped credit for large dividends). Foreign: 20% IBT before credit; US 30% WHT (no treaty) would fully absorb it.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 21% WHT on dividends to non-residents, reducible by treaty (corporate summary, not opened).
dividends.treaty_network: About 35 comprehensive agreements; no income tax treaty with the US (the 2025 US legislation to extend treaty benefits was not verified as in force).
dividends.holding_company_notes: CIT 20% plus 5% profit retention tax on undistributed earnings.

sources.title: Taiwan - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Land value tax 1%-5.5% of assessed land value (lower rate for owner-occupied residences, not verified) and house tax 1%-4.8% of assessed value for non-commercial buildings (PwC); luxury tax 10% on certain goods.

inheritance.summary: Estate tax applies to the estate (estate basis) at 10% up to TWD 56.21 million, 15% to TWD 112.42 million and 20% above (CPI-adjusted amounts, unchanged for 2026), after an exemption of TWD 13.33 million (Estate and Gift Tax Act art. 13, 18). For non-ROC nationals, and ROC nationals without habitual residence, only property located in Taiwan is taxed (arts. 1 and 3), and the deductions for a spouse, children, parents and others do not apply to them (art. 17, last paragraph); only the exemption does. Gift tax: 10%-20% after a TWD 2.44 million annual exemption per donor, same scope rule.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Estate exemption TWD 13.33 million per decedent, also for non-ROC nationals (art. 18). The family and other deductions (spouse TWD 5.53 million, TWD 560,000 per lineal descendant, parents, funeral) are for ROC nationals habitually resident in Taiwan only; art. 17 disapplies items 1-7 for non-ROC nationals and limits the funeral and debt deductions to Taiwan. Gift: TWD 2.44 million per donor per year.
inheritance.important_exceptions: A foreign family pays estate tax only on Taiwan-situs assets (e.g. a Taiwan home and Taiwan shares). ROC nationals are taxed worldwide if domiciled in Taiwan within two years before death or resident more than 365 days in those two years (Art. 4).

inheritance.spouse_note: For a decedent who is a non-ROC national or an ROC national living abroad, the spouse deduction (TWD 5.53 million for ROC residents) and the other family deductions of art. 17 items 1-7 do not apply (art. 17, last paragraph); the spouse is taxed like any other heir on Taiwan-situs property. Gifts between spouses are exempt, but gifts within two years of death are added back (art. 15).
inheritance.gift_tax: Gift tax 10% to TWD 28.11 million, 15% to 56.21 million, 20% above, after TWD 2.44 million per donor per year; non-nationals only on gifts of Taiwan property.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Nationality plus habitual residence (Art. 4): ROC nationals with a domicile in the two prior years or 365+ days of stay are taxed worldwide; non-nationals are always taxed on Taiwan property only. Amounts are indexed by law: art. 12-1 raises the exemption, bracket limits and deductions when the CPI has risen 10% or more since the last adjustment, from the following year, and the Ministry of Finance announces them each December (2026 amounts unchanged).

residency.tax_residency_test: Foreign individuals: resident if present 183 days or more in a calendar year. ROC nationals with household registration are resident if domiciled and habitually residing, unless the 31-day rule applies.

income.name: Taiwan

income_tax.summary: Resident individuals pay progressive tax of 5% to 40% (top rate above TWD 4.98m), plus an alternative minimum tax. Employees' own social insurance is small: labor insurance 2.3%, employment insurance 0.2% (both capped at TWD 45,800 monthly insured salary) and national health insurance about 1.55% (insured-salary cap TWD 313,000). The Employment Gold Card exempts 50% of salary above TWD 3m for up to five years.

employment_deduction.note: Salary special deduction of up to TWD 218,000 a person (or the salary if lower).

income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed contribution rules (occupational union, higher NHI share) could not be found on any opened page (NHI and Bureau of Labor Insurance pages returned 403/404), so the self-employed rate is a PLACEHOLDER equal to the employee NHI share and is not verified; the real cost is probably higher because the employer's share falls on the self-employed person.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Rates are for the 2025 return (filed 2026), the latest on PwC (page reviewed 20 August 2026); 2026 rates were not published. Allowance = personal exemption TWD 97,000 + standard deduction TWD 131,000 for a single filer; employees also get a salary special deduction of TWD 218,000 (not included). Alternative minimum tax: 20% on income above TWD 7.5m, payable if higher. Employee social insurance: labor insurance 11.5% x 20% = 2.3% and employment insurance 1% x 20% = 0.2% on insured salary up to TWD 45,800 a month (about TWD 1,145 a month), plus NHI 5.17% x 30% = 1.551% on insured salary up to TWD 313,000 a month; the recorded 1.551% rate and TWD 3,756,000 annual cap cover only NHI, so labor and employment insurance (small, capped) are excluded. Foreigners cannot join the labor pension.

succession.name: Taiwan
succession.summary: Children, spouse, parents, siblings and grandparents have a protected share of half or one third of their statutory share (Civil Code art. 1223). A foreign national's estate follows their national law. Taiwan has a Trust Act but is not in the Hague Trusts Convention, and foundations are public-interest only.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants, parents and spouse: one half of their statutory share; siblings and grandparents: one third (Civil Code art. 1223).
succession.foreign_law_note: Act Governing the Choice of Law in Civil Matters art. 58: succession is governed by the law of the deceased's nationality at death. A foreign national therefore keeps national law by default. I did not read the article text and a proviso for property in Taiwan may apply.
succession.trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table (Taiwan is not a party). The Trust Act (1996) and the Trust Enterprise Act allow trusts; the Estate and Gift Tax Act and the Income Tax Act tax trusts by type. Foundations (Civil Code arts. 59-65) need approval from the authority and serve public-benefit goals; family foundations are not available.
open_questions: Read the text of the choice-of-law Act art. 58 and any proviso.
Confirm the Trust Act's tax articles (Estate and Gift Tax Act art. 3-2).

assumptions: The family are EU citizens, not ROC nationals, resident in Taiwan 183 days or more; they have no Taiwan-source income (the home is owner-occupied) and no job or business.

All dividends and gains are foreign-source, so they reach tax only through the income basic tax (household basic income above TWD 7.5 million, 20%). Top rate assumed, as the real dividends (about EUR 600,000) are far above the thresholds.

The EUR 5M home is in Taiwan and is taxed in the estate at 10%-20% above TWD 13.33 million at each death (no family deductions for non-nationals); the inheritance check covers the foreign portfolio only.
Foreign dividends carry 15% withholding in the checks; US dividends would bear 30% (no US treaty), which exceeds the Taiwan tax and is lost.

Structures considered and rejected: a Taiwan holding company pays 20% CIT on worldwide income (Income Tax Act art. 3; PwC) and the 5% undistributed-earnings tax, then the owners pay 28% or the consolidated rate on payouts (art. 15), which is worse than the 20% basic tax on direct holding; a family trust is passed through to the beneficiary for income tax (art. 3-4), so it changes no rate, and the foreign assets of a non-national are outside estate tax in any case; an offshore company would be reached by the controlled foreign company rules (Income Basic Tax Act art. 12-1) and is not a Taiwan structure.
No special regime exists for a passive foreign family; the foreign-professional income relief is tied to employment.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the income basic tax gives each household a TWD 7.5 million deduction before the 20% (Income Basic Tax Act art. 13); the engine has no allowance, so it overstates the tax by TWD 1.5 million a household a year (1,500,000 in the check).

Needs an engine change: the Taiwan-situs family home is in the estate at each death (10%-20% above the TWD 13.33 million exemption, no family deductions for a non-national); the inheritance check carries only the foreign portfolio.
Check the 2027 amounts (IBT deduction, estate tax exemption and brackets) after the Ministry of Finance announcement in December 2026.

Estate tax amounts are CPI-indexed when prices rise 10% since the last change (art. 12-1); CPI was 11.49% above it in July 2026, so the exemption is likely to rise to about TWD 14.86M for 2027 (MOF announcement expected around year end).

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: A resident household (183 days) is taxed on foreign dividends and gains only through the income basic tax: 20% of basic income above TWD 7.5 million, once foreign income reaches TWD 1 million, less the foreign tax paid (Income Basic Tax Act arts. 12-13). Taiwan estate tax reaches only Taiwan-situs property of a non-ROC national (Estate and Gift Tax Act arts. 1, 17-18), so the foreign portfolio is outside it; the Taiwan home is not.
